method.label: Choose which gaps contain two ones

annotationRationale: Valid sequences correspond uniquely to choices of gaps containing two ones. Combinations count those choices, and addition combines the four exhaustive, disjoint zero-count cases.
sourceMethod: Followed the official alternative solution that splits by the number of zeros and chooses the gaps containing two ones. Added the inequalities establishing all possible cases and the inverse correspondence preventing duplicates.

review.mathCheck: With z zeros, the \(z-1\) intervening gaps contain one or two ones, so \(z-1\le19-z\le2(z-1)\), giving \(z=7,8,9,10\). Choosing the \(20-2z\) doubled gaps yields \(\binom66+\binom74+\binom82+\binom90=1+35+28+1=65\), choice C. The encoding handles both endpoints and is exhaustive and unique.
review.sourceMethodCheck: This is an independently worded, faithful adaptation of the second official solution on page 13. It retains the four zero-count cases and combination counts while explicitly justifying their bounds and the correspondence.
review.annotationCheck: Bijective counting and combinations are appropriately assessed; addition across mutually exclusive cases is support. The inverse encoding is explained, and the four cases neither omit nor repeat sequences.
